text: Community service work is a type of work that pays to improve a certain area or help a group of individuals. Many workers in community service are volunteers, though diverse non-profit and community organizations offer paid positions for people. Employees working in community services might provide different types of support to objects and places in a local area. There are many types of community service:
Some of the most personally satisfying careers exist in the community services sector.

**Community service workers** assist the elderly, children, and persons with disabilities to live better independent, secure, and rewarding lives by working with these vulnerable members of our society.
With their wide variety of professions, community services provide an intriguing and in-demand career path in an Australian industry that is still experiencing growth.
These are our **top 5 reasons for studying community services**, together with the salary you may expect and the necessary courses.
1. You want to affect people's lives truly
This is likely the most obvious purpose for individuals who work in **community service**.

Your help, support, and enthusiasm may help your clients improve and lead them to a better future. Working in this sector allows you the chance to have a significant effect on people's lives and make a meaningful difference.
It is very gratifying to know that someone is enjoying a fuller, happier life as a result of your impact!
2. You like variety in your career and being challenged

What does a **worker in community services do?** Plenty! A community service position places a strong emphasis on the **welfare and support of people** and involves a wide range of daily duties that call for a cheerful, patient, and encouraging attitude.
Health and well-being include anything from guiding your clients to choose nutritious foods and regular exercise to help them with dressing, cleaning, and other personal care tasks.
● **Daily Living Skills -** You will be on hand to assist several clients with daily living chores including grocery shopping, bill paying, and keeping a tidy, healthy home.
● **Advocacy-** Support their rights and make sure they are treated with respect and dignity while dealing with elderly or disabled clients who are at risk of exploitation.
● **Administration-** Maintaining client data is a significant administrative responsibility of community service positions, thus staying on top of reporting will be a daily or weekly task.

● **Being Able to Think Quickly Under Pressure-** You may also be asked to do client evaluations in person or over the phone during a crisis to ascertain their unique requirements. To offer food and clothes, you may need to make an emergency referral to medical services, psychiatric intervention, or support services. You may be required on the weekends, at night, and after work.
**There is Lots of Room to Move Around and Grow-** There is the freedom to move around and use your abilities because community services encompass such a wide range of work areas.
The industry may be divided into a number of sectors, including:
➢ Aged care
➢ Disability support
➢ Services for the rehabilitation of drug addicts
➢ Counselling and support for families
➢ Seeking asylum services
➢ Youth and child services
➢ Employment and training
➢ Housing options and related services
➢ Grief counseling

The majority of community service professions offer access to a wealth of on-the-job training to help you advance your career, and positions vary from entry-level to upper management and beyond.
3. Growing sector
To help them live their best lives, many Australians require compassionate care, encouragement, and instruction.

The largest employer in Australia is the Health Care and Social Assistance sector, which had about **1.7 million employees in 2018** and is expected to reach over **1.9 million by 2023**, according to the [Australian Skills and Industry Committee](https://nationalindustryinsights.aisc.net.au/industries/community-services).
Jobs in elderly care and personal care are in high demand thanks to an aging population; it is predicted that Australia will require **830,000 aged care employees by the year 2050**.

You'll need a [CHC33015-Certificate III in Individual Support](/course/certificate-iii-in-individual-support-ageing-home-and-community) to get started in this field. The next step is to decide whether to pursue more courses at the certificate IV, diploma, or bachelor's degree level in order to advance your abilities.\
4. You will develop important transferable skills
Building **beneficial transferrable skills** will pay off for you in both your professional and personal spheres of life.

Technical abilities will vary depending on the specific field you choose to work in, but soft skills are universal to all positions in this industry and involve taking responsibility and taking charge of others, working well in a team, problem-solving, critical analysis, and active listening.
Soft skills will give you an advantage in your next job interview and make you stand out from other candidates

Employers are increasingly searching for soft skills, according to LinkedIn's 2019 [Global Talent Trends](https://news.linkedin.com/2019/January/linkedin-releases-2019-global-talent-trends-report) study. A shortage of soft skills is cited as a problem by 91% of businesses, while 80% of businesses report having difficulty locating improved soft talents on the market.
Also, you'll be dealing with a variety of individuals on a regular basis, which, if you approach it the proper way, may contribute to the creation of a strong professional network for you.

How much you can earn as a community services worker?

items: On average, a community services officer makes $76,244 AUD annually.
An average social worker makes $81,058 AUD annually.
On average, a youth worker makes $34.85 AUD per hour.
On average, a carer makes $26.97 AUD per hour.
